Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure occurs because the test `testEscapeSurrogatePairs` exercises the method `StringEscapeUtils.escapeCsv` with a string containing a surrogate pair (`"\uD83D\uDE30"`). The call chain leads to `CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence input, Writer out)`. 

Inspecting this method reveals that it processes the input string character by character, attempting to translate from the current position. If nothing is translated (consume == 0), it writes the current code point to the output and advances by the length of the code point (which can be 1 or 2 chars for surrogate pairs).

However, if the consumed value from `translate(CharSequence input, int index, Writer out)` is larger than zero, it increments position in a loop using `Character.codePointAt(input, pos)` and `Character.charCount(...)`. This is expected to manage surrogate pairs correctly.

The issue likely lies in one of the translator implementations—such as the `CsvEscaper`—which inherits from `CharSequenceTranslator`. The actual `translate(CharSequence, int, Writer)` method in that class likely does not handle surrogate pairs properly, possibly reading past the end of the string, or miscalculating consumed chars resulting in `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

The provided snippet for `LookupTranslator.translate(...)` is a common implementation but does not show surrogate pair care; it tries to match subSequences and returns the matching length. When dealing with surrogate pairs, the method must not break surrogate pairs or exceed string length.

Thus, the root cause is that the escaping logic in `CharSequenceTranslator.translate(CharSequence, int, Writer)` or the subclass (like `CsvEscaper.translate(...)`) does not correctly handle surrogate pairs, resulting in `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when such pairs appear at the end or near the end of the input string. The contract states translators must understand code points but it appears they do not correctly segregate surrogate pairs.

Next, inspecting the `CsvEscaper.translate(...)` method or other relevant translator methods will confirm this.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
